newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean shares firmer but seen easing later.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean shares firmer but seen easing later.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrials traded firmer on Tuesday, buoyed by gains in a number of heavy-weight counters, but brokers predicted they would ease later in the week, saying the market generally remained "tired".

"I still see the market coming down. I think interest rates are still going to come up and that will take money to the money market from the stock market, which is still looking tired," one broker said.
"I see the index going below 10,000 soon, though some of the counters are getting cheaper," he added, saying this trend would probably rekindle investor interest in the bourse later on.

Tuesday's advancers included pharmaceutical firm Caps, up 115 cents to 2,525, while bankers Barclays added 100 cents to 2,800 and clothing retail group Edgars was 40 cents firmer at 750. Blue chip Delta, at 1,725, added 25 cents. The key index put on 54.10 points to 10,066.56.
Minings were quiet with gold giant Ashanti, copper miners Mhangura and coal producer Wankie all trading unchanged. The seven-share index there held steady at 1,009.05 for the third consecutive day.
